questions.question: How do register, handleSubmit, and formState.errors power React Hook Form — and when do you need Controller?
questions.title: React Hook Form
questions.direct_answer: RHF is uncontrolled by design: register('email') wires a ref + subscribes that field's validation; the form model lives in RHF's internal store, NOT React state — so typing doesn't re-render the component (only error-state updates for the fields you render). handleSubmit(validFn)(e) runs all validation, calls validFn(data) only when the whole form passes, and surfaces errors otherwise. formState.errors is the reactive error map — read it in the template to render per-field messages (subscribe via useForm's proxy: formState.errors.email updates only when email's state changes). Validation: rules in register ({ required, minLength, pattern }) or a schema (zod/yup via resolver) for cross-field and typed validation. Controller is the escape hatch for CONTROLLED components (design-system inputs that take value/onChange props and can't take a ref) — it renders the child with field props and bridges them into the same model.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    RG[register field: ref + rules + handlers] --> STORE[RHF internal model — not React state]
    STORE --> NR[typing: ~0 component re-renders]
    SUB[handleSubmit onValid onInvalid] --> V[run all validation]
    V -->|valid| OK[onValid typed data]
    V -->|invalid| ERR[formState.errors populated]
    ERR --> UI[render field messages — proxy-tracked]
    CTRL[controlled-only inputs: value/onChange no ref] --> C[Controller bridges them — costs per-keystroke renders]
    SCH[zod/yup resolver] --> CROSS[cross-field + typed validation at the boundary]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The formState proxy (the #1 real-world RHF bug): formState is a Proxy that RECORDS which properties your render reads — only those subscriptions fire re-renders. Destructure at the top of the component and you're fine (the proxy is read during render); but copy formState into a variable BEFORE render (or destructure inside a callback), and the subscription never registers — errors update in the store, your UI never re-renders. Related: subscribe() (v7.19+) is the explicit form for non-render consumption — watch/setState granularity without render coupling.

The resolver layer (schema validation in depth): zodResolver bridges a zod schema — validation moves from per-field rules to a single typed contract: const schema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), qty: z.number().min(1).max(9), confirm: z.string() }).refine(d => d.confirm === d.password, { message: 'must match', path: ['confirm'] }) — cross-field rules that register()'s per-field options can't express, plus the FORM DATA TYPE comes from the schema (useForm<z.infer<typeof schema>>), so onValid's data is fully typed with zero duplication. The trade: resolver validation runs the WHOLE schema per check (vs register's per-field short-circuit) — negligible for forms, worth knowing.

The reset/lifecycle surface (the integration points interviewers probe): reset(values) restores defaults (call it after a successful save or when props change — the standard 'form populated from server' pattern is useEffect + reset, NOT defaultValues that change later, which are only read on mount). unregister('field') removes dynamic fields. useFieldArray owns list-of-subfields (append/remove/move with keyed names notes.0.title — its whole job is stable identity under reorder, the React keys problem again). The one-liner worth closing with: RHF keeps the uncontrolled DOM fast path and adds exactly the reactive slice you render — that's the whole architecture.
